headline: 3,500 Democrats met in Denver to plan what's next.
summary: About 3,500 Democrats met in Denver this weekend, two weeks after winning Congress. The host, Majority Democrats, is a centrist group funded mostly by a billionaire couple. Likely 2028 candidates said the party should stop arguing over labels. Protesters heckled Hakeem Jeffries, and a left-wing news site was denied press passes.

cover_question.q: Why have a party after you win?

cover_answer: To plan the next game. And to argue a little.
table_question: After a win, should you celebrate first or get to work?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Two weeks ago one team of grown-ups, the Democrats, won a lot of elections. This weekend 3,500 of them met in Denver to celebrate and talk about what to do next, like a team meeting after the big game. A few people shouted at one of the leaders, and other people shouted back. Nobody got hurt, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: A team meeting after the big game. The shouting is one line, and it ends.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script gives one picture, a team meeting after the big game, and leaves out who paid for the room. The shouting gets one line because a child this age takes the loudest moment and reads your face before your words. Expect "who won?" The Democrats, two weeks ago.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Democrats just won Congress, and a group called Majority Democrats paid for their big meeting in Denver. Most of its money comes from one billionaire couple, and Democrats just ran against big money in politics. Like a team party paid for by one parent who then picks the plays.
8-12.why: Who paid, and what they get for it: a fairness chain.
8-12.why_long: At ten a child checks whether adults follow their own rules, so the script hands them the chain: the party ran against big money, won, then let a billionaire couple pay for the celebration. The parent who pays and picks the plays is a league they know. Expect "is that allowed?" Yes. The fight is over whether it looks right.

13-17.script: Does it matter who pays for the party if you won? Majority Democrats, funded mostly by one billionaire couple, hosted 3,500 Democrats in Denver after the party ran against big money and won. Second: it blocked a critical site's reporter, and the site gained readers. Who won that?
13-17.why: A win and a contradiction in one weekend.
13-17.why_long: A fourteen-year-old can hold two true things at once: the party won on a message against big money, and big money paid for the victory lap. Then the Lever episode, where blocking a reporter produced more readers. Expect "so is the group bad?" It says 3,500 people came. The critics say the room was bought. Both can be true.

5-7.q: Why have a party after you win?
5-7.a: To celebrate, and to plan what to do next. Teams do it after a big game.

8-12.a: A group called Majority Democrats, paid for mostly by one billionaire couple.
Health care, money in politics, and who leads Senate Democrats.

13-17.a: Josh Orton of Demand Justice says a fancy retreat doesn't fit the moment.
The Lever covers the group's funding. It was denied passes, then a reporter was blocked.
